title: EPAM SQL and PostgreSQL
description: SQL querying, joins, aggregation, subqueries, CTEs, database design, PostgreSQL JSON columns, EXPLAIN, transactions, and ORM performance.

questions.prompt: What is the core purpose of SELECT?
questions.explanation: SELECT describes what data to return from a table or query expression.

concept_panel.title: SELECT
concept_panel.explanation: SELECT describes what data to return from a table or query expression.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand basic SQL retrieval.

questions.prompt: Orders need customer emails. What SQL operation connects orders to users?
questions.explanation: JOINs combine related rows, usually through primary-key and foreign-key relationships.

concept_panel.title: JOINs
concept_panel.explanation: JOINs combine related rows, usually through primary-key and foreign-key relationships.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can query relational data.

questions.prompt: How do you calculate revenue per month?
options: GROUP BY month and aggregate amount
questions.answer: GROUP BY month and aggregate amount
questions.explanation: GROUP BY forms groups for aggregate functions such as SUM, COUNT, and AVG.

concept_panel.title: GROUP BY
concept_panel.explanation: GROUP BY forms groups for aggregate functions such as SUM, COUNT, and AVG.
concept_panel.practical_example: SELECT month, SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY month
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand aggregation.

questions.prompt: Where should you filter groups with SUM(amount) > 10000?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

concept_panel.title: HAVING
concept_panel.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand SQL execution semantics.

options: When a query needs the result of another query
questions.answer: When a query needs the result of another query
questions.explanation: Subqueries can compute intermediate sets or scalar values inside a larger query.

concept_panel.title: Subqueries
concept_panel.explanation: Subqueries can compute intermediate sets or scalar values inside a larger query.
concept_panel.practical_example: Find customers whose spend is above average.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can compose SQL logic.

options: To name an intermediate result for readability/reuse
questions.answer: To name an intermediate result for readability/reuse
questions.explanation: CTEs make complex SQL easier to read and can structure multi-step analysis.

concept_panel.title: CTEs
concept_panel.explanation: CTEs make complex SQL easier to read and can structure multi-step analysis.
concept_panel.practical_example: WITH monthly AS (...) SELECT * FROM monthly WHERE revenue > 0
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can write maintainable analytical SQL.

questions.prompt: What does a foreign key protect?
questions.explanation: Foreign keys prevent references to missing parent rows and document relationships.

concept_panel.title: Primary and Foreign Keys
concept_panel.explanation: Foreign keys prevent references to missing parent rows and document relationships.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you design relational schemas correctly.

questions.explanation: Normalization separates facts so updates happen in one place. It can increase joins, so design balances correctness and query needs.

concept_panel.title: Normalization
concept_panel.explanation: Normalization separates facts so updates happen in one place. It can increase joins, so design balances correctness and query needs.
concept_panel.practical_example: Store customer email once in users, not copied across every order.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand schema trade-offs.

questions.prompt: What does an index usually improve?
options: Read access for matching query patterns
questions.answer: Read access for matching query patterns
questions.explanation: Indexes speed lookups and ordering for supported access paths, but slow writes and use storage.

concept_panel.title: Indexes
concept_panel.explanation: Indexes speed lookups and ordering for supported access paths, but slow writes and use storage.
concept_panel.practical_example: Index orders(customer_id, created_at) for customer order history.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you reason about SQL performance.

questions.prompt: Why wrap a debit and credit in one transaction?
options: To commit both changes or neither
questions.answer: To commit both changes or neither
questions.explanation: Transactions protect invariants across multiple writes. ACID describes the guarantees.

concept_panel.title: Transactions and ACID
concept_panel.explanation: Transactions protect invariants across multiple writes. ACID describes the guarantees.
concept_panel.practical_example: Transfer money with debit and credit in one transaction.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you protect data correctness.

questions.prompt: When are PostgreSQL JSON columns useful?
options: For flexible attributes with known query/index trade-offs
questions.answer: For flexible attributes with known query/index trade-offs
questions.explanation: JSON columns add flexibility but can weaken constraints and complicate indexing if overused.

concept_panel.title: PostgreSQL JSON Columns
concept_panel.explanation: JSON columns add flexibility but can weaken constraints and complicate indexing if overused.
concept_panel.practical_example: Store integration metadata as JSON while core entities stay relational.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand PostgreSQL feature trade-offs.

questions.prompt: An endpoint suddenly gets slow. What should you inspect?
options: EXPLAIN plan and ORM lazy/eager loading behavior
questions.answer: EXPLAIN plan and ORM lazy/eager loading behavior
questions.explanation: EXPLAIN reveals scans, joins, and index usage. ORM lazy loading can create N+1 queries unless eager loading is chosen deliberately.

concept_panel.title: EXPLAIN and ORM Loading
concept_panel.explanation: EXPLAIN reveals scans, joins, and index usage. ORM lazy loading can create N+1 queries unless eager loading is chosen deliberately.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE plus selectinload for a slow relationship-heavy endpoint.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can debug database performance.

coding_challenges.title: EPAM SQL and PostgreSQL status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
